3.title: ちいさい「っ」・のばす　おと

kana.intro: A small っ is a short stop. A vowel written twice is one long sound.

cards.note: A small っ is a short stop: one beat of silence before the next sound. きって kitte, a stamp; without it, きて kite, come.
A vowel written twice is one long sound, two beats: おかあさん okāsan, mother. Short or long can change the word: おばさん obasan is an aunt, おばあさん obāsan a grandmother.
い after an i sound makes it long: おにいさん oniisan, older brother.
う after a u sound makes it long: くうき kūki, air.
A long e is mostly written えい: せんせい sensei, teacher. A few words write ええ: おねえさん onēsan, older sister.
A long o is mostly written おう: おとうさん otōsan, father. A few words write おお: おおきい ōkii, big.

kana.intro: Three kana are said another way when they are the little words of a sentence: は wa, を o, へ e.

kana.intro: Sounds and kana that are easy to mix up: the marks, small and big kana, and long sounds.

cards.note: が has the two small strokes ゛; か does not. かぎ, a key; かき, a persimmon.
ば has the two small strokes ゛ and is ba; ぱ has the small circle ゜ and is pa.
A big つ is the sound tsu. A small っ is a short stop: くつ kutsu, shoes; きって kitte, a stamp.
びよういん has five beats, び・よ・う・い・ん: a hair salon. びょういん has four, びょ・う・い・ん: a hospital.
Short or long: おばさん obasan is an aunt, おばあさん obāsan a grandmother.
ぢ and づ sound just like じ and ず. Most words use じ and ず: ちず, a map. A few use づ: つづく, to go on.
